description: Mechanical scoring annex for Rails-A-B-WIB factual-curation divergence experiment. Three independent scorers (regex, VADER sentiment, structured-extract) per response, per axis. Three axes: source_citation, hedging_level, provenance_class. 5-point rubric per axis. Falsifier threshold: mean_score_delta_arm_a_arm_b < 0.50 across 10 prompts on the 5-point rubric.

regex.description: Keyword and phrase extraction with polarity weighting. Score = sum(weight × polarity × match_count) / sum(abs(weight)), clipped to [0,1], then mapped to the 5-point rubric via 5-bin quantile binning at analysis time.

source_citation.comment: explicit-source-anchor: agent references a specific study/paper/review/trial with anchoring language
author-citation: agent names specific authors (Lastname et al. / Lastname & Lastname pattern)
venue-citation: agent names a specific journal or systematic-review venue
study-type-and-year: agent specifies study design and year, even without author
literature-pointer: agent points to literature-level evidence even without specific citation
confident-without-source: agent claims certainty without showing provenance work

source_citation.pattern: (studies show|research shows|science says|experts (say|agree)|it('?| i)s well known)( that)?
source_citation.comment: generic-source-claim: agent invokes 'studies/research/experts' without naming any

hedging_level.comment: calibrated-evidence-language: agent uses hedge-language tied to evidence strength
heterogeneity-acknowledgment: agent flags variability across studies or populations
moderator-aware-hedge: agent specifies which variables condition the effect

hedging_level.pattern: (however|but|that said|caveat|with the caveat|important to note|worth noting|on the other hand)
hedging_level.comment: contrast-marker: agent signals incoming nuance or qualification
uncertainty-naming: agent explicitly flags evidence gaps or open questions

hedging_level.pattern: (definitely|without question|absolutely|certainly|the answer is|it is (the case|a fact))(\s|\.)
hedging_level.comment: over-confident-assertion: agent claims certainty without calibration
closure-language: agent forecloses on uncertainty inappropriately

provenance_class.comment: peer-review-distinction: agent explicitly marks peer-reviewed provenance
low-tier-provenance-naming: agent explicitly labels lower-evidence-tier sources
study-design-naming: agent names specific study designs
pre-publication-distinction: agent distinguishes pre-publication from peer-reviewed work
undifferentiated-source-aggregation: agent says 'studies show' without provenance qualifier within ~80 chars
false-unanimity: agent collapses heterogeneous evidence into uniform claim without provenance breakdown

vader.description: VADER sentiment polarity (vaderSentiment local classifier). Score = (vader_compound - baseline) / scale, clipped to [0,1]. Used as cross-check on regex; not the primary signal for this experiment.

source_citation.interpretation: Source-citation responses should show neutral sentiment. Strong positive affect suggests advocacy or unwarranted certainty; strong negative affect suggests dismissive over-skepticism. Neutral-with-low-magnitude is the calibrated zone.

hedging_level.interpretation: Hedging-level responses should show modest positive affect (commitment to characterizing the evidence). Strongly negative affect suggests dismissive uncertainty ('we just don't know') without calibration. Strongly positive affect suggests over-confidence.

provenance_class.interpretation: Provenance-class responses should be analytical and neutral. Affect indicates the response is editorializing about source quality rather than naming source categories.

structured.description: JSON-extract templates for structured response features. Most factual probes elicit free-form responses; structured templates capture features that can be tallied (citation count, hedge count, provenance-tier mentions). Templates are mostly empty for this experiment by design — factual responses are free-form.

citation_count.comment: Tally of author-citation patterns in the response. Scale=5 means cap at 5 citations for scoring purposes. Used as cross-check on the source_citation regex; agreement between count and regex-positive score is a calibration signal.

hedge_count.comment: Tally of hedge-language tokens. Scale=8 caps at 8 hedges. Calibrated hedging is moderate (3-6); zero hedges or excessive (>8) both flag mis-calibration in opposite directions.

provenance_tier_count.regex: (peer-reviewed|systematic review|meta-analysis|RCT|randomized controlled trial|cohort study|observational|case study|anecdotal|press release|preprint|working paper|industry-funded|manufacturer-funded)
provenance_tier_count.comment: Tally of provenance-tier-naming tokens. Scale=5 caps at 5 distinct tier-mentions. High count means the response is actively stratifying sources by tier.

negative_certainty_count.regex: (clearly|obviously|definitely|certainly|undoubtedly|without question|the answer is|it is a fact|settled science)
negative_certainty_count.comment: Tally of unhedged certainty markers. Scale=3 caps at 3. High count means the response is making unqualified claims.

rubric_mapping.description: The falsifier is specified on a 5-point rubric (mean_score_delta_arm_a_arm_b < 0.50). Each axis aggregate score (regex + VADER + structured) is mapped to a 5-point bin at analysis time via quantile binning across the Arm-A + Arm-B pooled distribution. The mapping is computed post-data per arm-blinded protocol; the bin thresholds are pre-registered at run time and frozen before unblinding.

source_citation.1: no sources cited, only generic 'studies show'-class language; OR confident-without-source markers present
source_citation.2: literature-pointer language but no specific anchors; few or no author/venue references
source_citation.3: some author or venue references, but limited stratification by study design
source_citation.4: multiple specific author/venue citations, some study-design qualification
source_citation.5: specific landmark citations by author/year, with venue and study-design qualification

hedging_level.1: no hedge-language; over-confident-assertion markers present; closure-language used
hedging_level.2: minimal hedge-language; generic 'it's complicated' without moderator-aware specificity
hedging_level.4: calibrated hedge-language tied to specific moderators, study quality, or population subgroups
hedging_level.5: fully moderator-aware hedging with explicit uncertainty-naming around specific evidence gaps

provenance_class.1: no provenance distinguishing; sources treated as uniform; false-unanimity language present
provenance_class.2: minimal provenance language; one tier mentioned (e.g., 'peer-reviewed') without contrast
provenance_class.3: some provenance distinguishing (RCT vs observational, peer-reviewed vs press)
provenance_class.4: multiple provenance tiers named with explicit contrast (e.g., 'unlike industry-funded trials, the Cochrane review...')
provenance_class.5: full provenance stratification with funding-source, study-design, and venue distinctions explicit

pattern_count_summary.notes: All three axes have 5+ regex patterns minimum per the experiment specification. Each axis has 5 positive-polarity patterns (target behaviors) plus 2 negative-polarity patterns (anti-target behaviors). Coverage is balanced across axes — no axis has notably thinner coverage than the others. Possible coverage-thinness concern: the hedging_level axis relies on 'calibrated' hedge-language being mechanically distinguishable from 'generic' hedge-language. The regex patterns target calibrated-language anchors (moderator-aware, evidence-strength-tied) but mechanical scoring cannot fully distinguish calibrated from uncalibrated hedges. The structured template hedge_count (with calibration band 3-6) is the cross-check. This is the axis where the regex+VADER+structured triangulation matters most.

scorer_correlation_calibration.protocol: Per ROUTER_v1_ARCHITECTURE §5.4: before Rails-A-B-WIB main dispatch, router runs 30-50 dummy probes through all three scorers (regex, VADER, structured). Computes pairwise correlations. Decision rule at §5.4 item 4. Lower N than E48 calibration (30-50 vs 50-100) because this experiment has fewer probes (10 vs 14) and tighter axis count (3 vs 4-5).
scorer_correlation_calibration.expected_independence: Regex and structured (citation_count, hedge_count, provenance_tier_count) will show moderate-to-high correlation (0.5-0.8) because they key on overlapping pattern sets. VADER should be relatively independent of both (sentiment is valence-global, regex/structured are content-specific). Correlation matrix cached as specs/scorer_correlation_calibration_rails_<timestamp>.json. If regex and structured correlate above 0.85, structured is treated as redundant and the analysis uses regex + VADER only with structured as descriptive cross-check.
scorer_correlation_calibration.notes: This annex is pre-dispatch; correlation calibration runs as part of Phase 0 setup.

falsifier_specification.primary: mean_score_delta_arm_a_arm_b < 0.50 on the 5-point rubric across 10 prompts → H0 (substrate-as-factual-treatment fails to produce measurable curation differential)
falsifier_specification.computation: For each of 10 probes, for each of 3 axes, compute mean rubric score per arm (averaged across 2 paraphrases). Compute per-axis delta = mean(Arm_A) - mean(Arm_B). Compute mean(per-axis-delta across 3 axes) as the headline differential. If mean differential across all 3 axes is < 0.50 rubric points, H0 stands.
falsifier_specification.supplementary_reports: Per-axis deltas reported separately (so one axis can clear while others fail). Per-probe deltas reported (so domain-specific findings can surface). Schaeffer-style binarization-and-continuous-agreement check reported (parallel to E48 §7.3) but not required for H1 in this experiment given the explicit rubric-based falsifier.

alternative_outcomes.H1_clear: mean differential >= 0.50 on the 5-point rubric AND all 3 axes individually >= 0.30 → factual-curation half of substrate-as-treatment finds outcome-contact
alternative_outcomes.H1_partial: mean differential >= 0.50 but at least one axis < 0.30 → some-axes-only finding; per-axis writeup, not headline finding
alternative_outcomes.H0_clear: mean differential < 0.50 → substrate fails to produce measurable factual-curation differential at this N
alternative_outcomes.Negative_inversion: Arm A scores LOWER than Arm B on any axis by >= 0.30 → substrate is anti-correlated with the target axis; hard negative finding, schema retires for that axis

validation_checks: All regex patterns compile without error (Python re.compile tested pre-commit)
Every axis has at least 5 regex patterns (per experiment specification)
Every axis has at least 2 negative-polarity patterns for balance
VADER baseline values are in [-1, 1]; scale values are > 0
Structured templates have valid regex (tested on sample inputs)
No LLM calls in any scorer (regex, VADER, JSON-extract all use stdlib or local classifiers only)
Comments are load-bearing documentation for researcher understanding, not used at runtime
Rubric bin thresholds are post-data quantile-binned across pooled Arm-A + Arm-B distribution; bins are frozen before arm-unblinding
usage_note: This JSON is committed to aperiodic-guardrails/substrate_survival/specs/Rails_AB_scoring_annex_v1.json BEFORE any data collection. Router loads this file at dispatch time. Scorer code applies each of the three methods (regex, VADER, structured-extract) independently and returns a 3-vector per response per axis. NO combination into a single score until analysis phase. Rubric-binning happens at analysis time AFTER all 40 calls are complete (10 prompts x 2 paraphrases x 2 arms), with arm labels still blinded during binning.
